name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A vehicle intended for off-highway use, including all-terrain vehicles, utility-terrain vehicles and motorcycles, all of which West Virginia's ATV rules cover; an electric dirt bike like a Sur-Ron or Talaria ridden off-road is one.

restrictions.rule: Intended for off-highway use; no limit on motor power or speed
Riders under 18 need a certificate from a DMV-offered or approved rider safety awareness course, except on a recreational trail or area run by an entity with its own safety program
Riders under 18 must wear a helmet meeting FMVSS 218, ANSI Z90.1 or Snell standards
No passenger under 18 unless the operator is 18 or older or holds at least a Level II intermediate license
Needs a lit headlight and taillight from sunset to sunrise, and a spark arrester and muffler

Never allowed on an interstate, and on a road with a center line or more than two lanes only to cross it at a right angle after stopping, or for up to 10 miles on the shoulder at 25 mph or less between a residence or lodging and riding areas
On the Hatfield-McCoy Trails, every rider needs a trail user permit and a DOT or Snell helmet
Cities may regulate or ban it on city streets, and counties on non-interstate roads if they operate under a countywide comprehensive plan, or within a homeowners' association's area on its petition
Most of these rules don't apply on the owner's land or private land ridden with permission, except the passenger, helmet and safety-course rules
